source: Hand labels for L3 (Wave 2, V5), drafted for the Lead to verify: each idea was written fresh against the reference fix in the corpus _solutions dir, never graded before, without reading any recorded grader verdict; near misses touch the hot code or its module but leave the reference root cause in place.

labels.title: Test tags against a set built from the allowlist once
labels.rationale: count_by_kind hands the allowlist list to matches, and every `tag in allowed` scans that list from its start. Turn the allowlist into a set once at the top of count_by_kind and pass the set, so each membership test is a hash lookup; the counts stay identical.
labels.label: hit
labels.why: The reference fix's cost: list membership in matches, replaced by a set built once per count_by_kind call.

labels.title: Inline matches into the count_by_kind loop
labels.rationale: count_by_kind calls matches once per record and pays a Python function call each time. Inline the tag loop into count_by_kind so no call is made per record; the counts stay identical.
labels.label: miss
labels.why: Same hot code, wrong cost: it saves the call overhead, but each tag is still tested by scanning the allowlist list, which is what the reference removes.

labels.title: Compile the whole-word keyword pattern once per scan
labels.rationale: hits_by_level calls mentions for every log line, and mentions sorts, escapes and joins the keywords and compiles the regular expression again each time. Build the compiled pattern once in hits_by_level and search every line with it; whole-word matching and the counts do not change.
labels.label: hit
labels.why: Exactly the reference fix: the per-line pattern build and compile hoisted to one per hits_by_level call.

labels.title: Order the keyword alternatives longest first
labels.rationale: mentions joins the sorted keywords into one alternation. Ordering the alternatives by descending length lets the regular expression engine settle on a whole-word match with less backtracking; the matched lines stay the same.
labels.label: miss
labels.why: Changes what the pattern holds, but the pattern is still rebuilt and compiled for every line, the cost the reference hoists.

labels.title: Read the current hop count once per dequeued node
labels.rationale: hops reads distance[node] again for every neighbour it discovers. Read it once into a local after taking the node off the pending list and reuse it for every target, saving a dictionary lookup per edge; the distances do not change.
labels.label: miss
labels.why: A per-edge saving inside the same loop; the pending list still pays pop(0), which shifts every element, the cost the reference removes with a deque.

labels.title: Tally word frequencies in a single pass
labels.rationale: frequencies calls words.count for each distinct word, so the whole word list is walked once per distinct word. Walk the list once, adding one to a per-word counter in a dict (or a collections.Counter), then return the entries in sorted word order; the mapping is the same.
labels.label: hit
labels.why: The reference fix: one counting pass instead of a list.count scan per distinct word.

labels.title: Select the most common words with a heap
labels.rationale: most_common sorts every distinct word only to keep the first limit of them. Use heapq.nsmallest(limit, ...) with the same (-count, word) key so only the top entries are ordered; ties stay in alphabetical order.
labels.label: miss
labels.why: Same module, other function: most_common's sort is not the cost; frequencies' repeated words.count scans stay in place.

labels.title: Track seen SKUs with an insertion-ordered dict
labels.rationale: distinct_skus checks `line.sku not in seen` against a growing list for every shipment line. Keep the first-seen order with dict.fromkeys over the SKUs (or a set beside the list) so each check takes constant time; the SKUs come out in the same order.
labels.label: hit
labels.why: Root cause 1 (catalog.py): the list membership scan in distinct_skus, removed as the part1 patch does.

labels.title: Map each order number to its rank once
labels.rationale: arrival_ranks calls numbers.index(line.order_id) for every line, a linear search of the sorted order numbers. Build a dict from order number to its position once and look every line up in it; the ranks do not change.
labels.label: hit
labels.why: Root cause 2 (orders.py): list.index per line replaced by a rank dict, as the part2 patch does.

labels.title: Total warehouse units with a defaultdict
labels.rationale: units_by_warehouse calls totals.get with a default for every shipment line. A collections.defaultdict(int) avoids the get call per line; the totals and their sorted order do not change.
labels.label: miss
labels.why: Same module as root cause 1 but a linear function that is not a hot spot; neither the SKU list scan nor the index search is touched.

labels.title: Insert each pickup offer at its sorted place
labels.rationale: pending_views copies and re-sorts the whole pending list every time one offer arrives. Find the new offer's position with a binary search and insert it there, keeping the list in ascending order without sorting it again; the recorded views do not change.
labels.label: hit
labels.why: Root cause 3 (pickups.py): the full re-sort per offer replaced by a sorted insert, as the part3 patch does with insort.

labels.title: Memoise leg_length per pair of stops
labels.rationale: leg_length is called once per leg of the round. Cache its result per (from, to) pair with functools.lru_cache so no pair of stops is measured twice; every length stays the same.
labels.label: miss
labels.why: Same module as root cause 2 but its constant-time distance, not distance_so_far's re-summing of every prefix; the stop scan and the re-sort stay too.
